name: Conversational Settings
description: Lets users edit module settings via natural language — TPM parses the request, identifies the target setting, and either proposes the change or applies it directly via the settings-write verb, gated by Application Mode and the Enable Settings Write master switch. Phase 1: scalar settings only.

enableDetection.label: Enable Detection
enableDetection.description: Master switch for natural-language settings detection. When on, TPM watches user turns for settings-edit intent. When off, settings must be edited directly via the Modules tab.

triggerPhrases.label: Trigger Phrases
triggerPhrases.description: Comma-separated, case-insensitive substrings suggesting settings-edit intent. Broad phrases (set, change) may over-trigger; the downstream fuzzy-match step usually filters false positives.
triggerPhrases.default: turn on, turn off, enable, disable, set, change, raise, lower, switch, flip, toggle, update setting, configure

applicationMode.label: Application Mode
applicationMode.description: How TPM responds to a recognized settings-edit intent. propose (default): surfaces the exact panel edit for the user to apply manually. apply: applies directly via settings-write (falls back to propose if Enable Settings Write is off or the host refuses). ask: prompts per occurrence. Independent of Enable Settings Write — this alone never writes anything.

enableSettingsWrite.label: Enable Settings Write
enableSettingsWrite.description: Off by default — set-module-setting is refused for every request regardless of Application Mode. On doesn't itself cause a write: Application Mode must also be apply (or ask-then-apply), and every write remains subject to host checks (schema, self-reference denylist, the mode.ticket-pr/War Mode bar).

requireConfirmationFor.label: Require Confirmation For
requireConfirmationFor.description: Comma-separated setting categories requiring explicit confirmation before a change. all means everything; other tags (secrets, allowlists, modes) name recognized categories. Tighten to skip confirmation on routine settings.

fuzzyMatchThreshold.label: Fuzzy Match Threshold
fuzzyMatchThreshold.description: Confidence percent required to act on a fuzzy-matched setting name. Raise for stricter matching (fewer false positives, more clarifying prompts); lower for more permissive matching.
